newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish leaders gather for military meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turkish leaders gather for military meeting.

text.p: Turkey's political and military leaders gathered on Saturday for a meeting of the National Security Council that was expected to deal with planned curbs on religious activism that have badly damaged the government.
Pressure from the military-dominated council to impose strict secularist directives has caused a rift in Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition with conservatives.

Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, was among dignitaries at a ceremony on Saturday to mark the council's founding in the 1930s. The event appeared to be aimed at boosting the army's profile ahead of the monthly meeting.

"Since the day it came to power, our government has given priority to the strategic issues recommended by the National Security Council and made an effort to put them into force," the prime minister said in a speech at the ceremony.
The government has done little to implement the council's demands for an anti-Islamist crackdown, including planned restrictions on religious education and traditional Islamic dress.

Erbakan's reluctance to act against his own grassroots has angered his conservative True Path Party coalition allies. A True Path MP resigned on Friday, costing the government its absolute majority in parliament.

Erbakan and True Path leader Tansu Ciller were unable to agree on True Path proposals for formation of an "election government" to lead the country to early polls at three hours of talks on Friday. More talks are expected at the weekend.
